```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Six simulated cohorts share two co-expressed programs: genes 1-40 drive response, genes 101-300 do not. Two
signatures cover the first program; a third samples the second, and a fourth is noise.

```{r simulate-and-run}
library(decoyfdr)
set.seed(1)
genes <- sprintf("G%03d", 1:400)
cohorts <- lapply(1:6, function(i) {
  f <- rnorm(60)
  X <- matrix(rnorm(400 * 60), 400, 60, dimnames = list(genes, sprintf("c%d_%02d", i, 1:60)))
  X[1:40, ] <- X[1:40, ] + matrix(f, 40, 60, byrow = TRUE)
  X[101:300, ] <- X[101:300, ] + matrix(rnorm(60), 200, 60, byrow = TRUE)
  y <- rbinom(60, 1, plogis(1.2 * f)); names(y) <- colnames(X)
  dfdr_cohort(X + 5, y, name = paste0("C", i))
})
lib <- dfdr_library(list(prog_a = genes[1:20], prog_b = genes[21:40], other = genes[101:115],
                         noise = genes[320:340]),
                    engine = "mean", direction = c(prog_a = 1, prog_b = 1, other = 1, noise = 1))
res <- run_decoy_fdr(cohorts, lib, n_coex = 8, n_rand = 2, n_sets = 3, n_draw = 200, keep_draws = 100, seed = 7, B = 500)
res$decoys$info[res$decoys$info$class == "coex", c("target", "r_target_med", "r_achieved_med")][c(1, 9, 17, 25), ]
res
subset(res$calls, kind == "target")
```

The two signatures of the response program are called. Their co-expressed decoys, grown from genes in no
signature, take their co-expression from the unrelated program and are not called, so the estimated FDR is low.
The estimate pools three independent decoy sets here (the default is ten, as in the paper); `fdr_set_min` and
`fdr_set_max` give the range of the per-set estimates. The plain estimate sums the decoy call rate over every
target, true ones included, so it is the estimate with pi0 = 1; `fdr_pi0` multiplies it by the share of targets
whose statistic does not stand out from their own decoys':

```{r estimates}
res$fdr[, c("stat", "class", "called", "fdr", "fdr_lo", "fdr_hi", "fdr_set_min", "fdr_set_max", "pi0", "fdr_pi0")]
```
Under permuted outcomes every call is false, and the decoys estimate how many there are:

```{r global-null}
calibrate_null(res$fit, B = 100, seed = 8)$summary
```
